Soundcore by Anker P20i True Wireless Earbuds

amazon -

These wireless earbuds give you up to 10 hours of listening on a charge and 30 hours total when you factor in the charging case. The companion app lets you choose from 22 EQ presets and customize the controls, while a Find My Earbuds feature can help when one inevitably disappears into the couch. They're also water-resistant and have two microphones designed to make calls sound clearer.

49% Off A Hydrating Serum With An Easy Twist & Click Applicator

medicube Collagen Glow Booster Serum

-

Amazon -

Nourishing your skin has never been easier, thanks to this deeply hydrating serum in a handy click pen applicator. The formula features hero ingredients like niacinamide, milk protein, and collagen, and it's backed by a 4.5-star overall rating.

63% Off A Pair Of Memory-Foam Slippers With A Nonslip Sole

EverFoams Fuzzy Slippers

amazon -

Give cold feet a softer place to land with these plush indoor slippers. They have a fuzzy wool-like upper, a soft lining, and memory-foam cushioning underfoot, while the nonslip sole adds some extra grip around the house. They're even machine washable, which is a nice perk for something you may end up wearing every day.

57% Off An Iconic Soft Cotton Bralette With Over 22,000 5-Star Reviews

Calvin Klein Modern Cotton Unlined Wireless Bralette

amazon -

This wireless, unlined bralette is made from a soft cotton-modal blend with stretch, giving it a lightweight and breathable feel for everyday wear. The pullover racerback silhouette keeps things simple, while the wide elastic band adds support without an underwire. It's machine washable, and Amazon recommends sizing up if you prefer more coverage or a more relaxed fit.

60% Off A Ring Battery Doorbell With 2K Video

Ring Battery Doorbell

amazon -

Upgrade your front-door setup with this rechargeable Ring doorbell, which gives you a wide-angle view in sharp 2K video. Two-Way Talk lets you communicate with someone at your door, while enhanced zoom makes it easier to take a closer look at what's happening outside. Because the battery is built in and rechargeable, you don't need to rely on existing doorbell wiring.

41% Off Super Comfy, Cushioned Pillow Slides

Joomra Pillow Slippers

-

amazon -

True to their name, the 1.7-inch-deep sole of these slippers ensures a cloud-like, pillowy feel with every step. The deep heel cups and nonslip bottoms help improve grip, making them comfortable to walk in around the house or out on errands. Made of waterproof and quick-drying EVA material, they're lightweight; you can even use a hair dryer to heat them before wearing them for the first time (as described in the listing) for a completely custom fit.

46% Off A Cult-Favorite Snail Mucin Essence

COSRX Snail Mucin Repairing Serum

amazon -

This lightweight essence uses 96.3% snail secretion filtrate to give dry or dull-looking skin a boost of hydration. It's designed to absorb without leaving behind a heavy feel while helping skin look smoother, healthier, and more glowy. More than 100,000 Amazon shoppers have weighed in on it, and it maintains an impressive rating of over 4.5 stars.

25% Off A Tinted Mineral Sunscreen With SPF 50

La Roche-Posay Anthelios Mineral Light Fluid Sunscreen

-

amazon -

This SPF 50 sunscreen uses a 100% mineral formula and was developed with sensitive skin in mind. Its lightweight, tinted texture is designed to blend into skin quickly and leave behind a matte, healthy-looking finish instead of a heavy layer. With more than 30,000 reviews, it’s a popular option for adding daily sun protection without making your morning routine feel more complicated.

20% Off The Best-Selling Mighty Patch Pimple Patches

Mighty Patch Hero Cosmetics Original Pimple Patches (36 Count)

Amazon -

These pimple patches are a best-seller for a reason. They work overnight, utilizing hydrocolloid to pull pus out of whiteheads and speed up healing... no painful popping involved.

27% Off A Clever Outlet Extender That Doubles As A Night Light

POWRUI Multi-Plug Wall Outlet Night Light

Amazon -

This wall outlet can power up to nine electronics simultaneously (there are three USB ports and six standard outlets spread among three sides). And there's even a built-in night light that puts out a soft, warm glow for visibility.

67% Off A Color-Changing Foundation

Luxe Color-Changing Foundation

-

amazon -

Trying to find the right foundation shade from your screen is near impossible — which is why this genius pH-based formula comes in three color-changing shades that go on white and then shift to your skin tone for a perfect match. Designed to avoid settling into fine lines, it smooths, hydrates, and evens out discoloration via niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, vitamin E, and more. It leaves behind a matte finish and blends effortlessly for a seamless look.

item.title: Spicy Books Like 'The Hunting Wives' With Drama & Mystery
item.description: Now that 'The Hunting Wives' Season 2 has arrived, here are five spicy books with similar themes — from small-town sapphic romances to friendship murder mysteries.
item.dc:creator: Grace Wehniainen
item.content:encoded:
Happy Thanksgiving, indeed: The Hunting Wives Season 2 arrives just in time for the holiday season.

Based on May Cobb’s novel of the same name, the hit Netflix series follows a group of small-town Texas women who cultivate friendship — and sometimes a little more — against a backdrop of killer small-town scandal.

So buzzy is the series starring Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow that a third season is officially on the way. But if you’ve already breezed through the latest episodes and can’t wait for more, there’s no shortage of steamy page-turners that you’ll enjoy just as much in the meantime.

Whether you’re looking for small-town sapphic romance, friendship mysteries, or swoony country settings that make you want to slip into your cowgirl boots, here are five spicy books to read after The Hunting Wives.

Ribbonwood by Ruby Landers

Lara happily plays the part of Ribbonwood’s social pariah. But from the shadows, she uses her scandalous reputation as a cover for helping women break free from the bad men in their lives — cobbling together a close-knit group of friends who become family over bonfire nights. When her former high-school rival Ollie returns to their small Australian hometown, the women forge a steamy relationship that catches them both off-guard.

Wild Love by Elsie Silver

If the cowgirl trappings of The Hunting Wives have you craving further country spice, you’ll devour Wild Love. The first of Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill series (an adaptation is coming to Prime Video!) follows wealthy music executive Ford and his irresistible connection with his best friend’s sister, Rosie, all set in a charming small town nestled in the Canadian Rockies.

One of Us Is Dead by Jeneva Rose

From her exclusive salon, Jenny gets a front-row seat to the toxic drama afflicting the wealthy housewives of Atlanta’s Buckhead neighborhood. But she’s more than professionally invested in the lives of her clients, especially when one of them is murdered.

Bloom Town: Genesis by Ally North

Like Sophie and Margo, this sapphic love story plays out amid major criminal activity. Female outlaw Joey kidnaps preacher’s daughter Abby on a train ride out west in the 1850s, but before long, the mission gives way to a passionate and eye-opening romance.

Zetas Till We Die by Amber & Danielle Brown

A group of sorority sisters reunites 10 years after one of their own was killed. But as the novel hops between then and now, you realize with the Zetas that the truth of Lupé’s death is murkier than it first appeared.

item.title: Why I Miss The Chaos Of 2000s Black Friday. Sort Of.
item.description: Before online shopping took over, 2000s mall Black Friday was a chaotic communal ritual. Here’s why I miss the madness — and why I’m glad it’s gone.
item.dc:creator: Morgan Sullivan
item.content:encoded:
There’s a particularly poignant line in Taylor Swift’s catalog that scratches my brain every time I hear it. It’s off her Evermore track “Coney Island,” where she likens a failed relationship to “the mall before the internet,” calling it “the one place to be.”

It’s one of those lines I’ll always restart the song for. The lyric evokes such vivid memories. While some people conjure up an ex when they hear it, I picture the mall itself. Because I miss it. Like, genuinely, embarrassingly, more than I miss some people I’ve dated.

My longing for the mall becomes even stronger during the holidays. When red cup season returns and TikTok-certified gift guides hit the FYP, I’m reminded of what we lost: clipping and circling newspaper inserts for deals, lining up before dawn for the latest, hottest thing, and arguing with your cousins over who gets it if there’s only one left. In other words, Black Friday. True Black Friday — not just the predominantly digital version. Because the spectacle of the true doorbuster seems to no longer exist.

Though it was a hectic corporate holiday (and, admittedly, a nightmare for anyone working a retail shift), Black Friday was, in many ways, a rare cultural victory. There was a real in-it-together feeling. You’d strategize with your sister or cousins, mapping out your plan of action together as Thanksgiving dinner wrapped up. When the last dish had been loaded into the dishwasher, you knew your next move: more consumption. General consumerism, to be clear.

Because you *needed* that new Jessica Simpson coat from Macy’s, and you’d gladly line up at 4 a.m. if it meant getting it for 80% off. So you and your family would down Red Bulls late Thursday night — or maybe it was coffee, whatever — just to stay awake until it was time to roll out. The drink didn't matter; what mattered was that you were going to experience the whole marathon together.

Perhaps that butterfly feeling was what made Black Friday so special, and not the deals per se. Because, TBH, as a chronic shopper, I find that most online deals today are better than they were IRL in the 2000s.

Nonetheless, you’d jump into the car, blast a burned CD of holiday hits (with Mariah Carey’s "All I Want for Christmas Is You" blaring, so not all has changed), and the magical feeling of the season wafted through the air. Or maybe it was just the relief of actual air, because you all were wearing thick, itchy Thanksgiving sweaters, smooshed into your sister’s Honda Civic, and it was feeling irrationally hot. You’d come to find, of course, that the mall would be no different, temperature-wise.

I never thought I’d see a fight break out over toys in the middle of a suburban food court, yet there we were.

So, maybe that wasn’t the magic either. Maybe it was the chatting with strangers in line outside of Walmart or Best Buy, trying to figure out whether they were hunting for the same thing — quietly sizing them up to see if they were, in fact, the enemy. Because as soon as those doors opened, they were, especially if they had their eye on a wool coat, too.

The chaos that ensued felt like a designer sample sale straight out of Confessions of a Shopaholic, or like the shopping scenes from Jingle All the Way. I never thought I’d see a fight break out over toys in the middle of a suburban food court, yet there we were.

It was dazzling and overwhelming all at once: a visual overload, with the suffocatingly sweet cloud of Victoria’s Secret’s rich, floral gourmand “Love Spell” wafting through the crowds. The night was equal parts exhilarating and anxiety-inducing, with arms loaded down with bags, mental math happening in real time, and the inevitable, “Wait — you’re working tonight?! HOW!?” blurted out before your best friend was ushered away into the madness.

That physical madness is a stark contrast to how we compete for things now. The last time I realized we really were still a monoculture was when I tried to get Slayyyter tickets this year. I’d forgotten we all basically like the same stuff. Waiting in a virtual queue, Ticketmaster-style, made me realize what we’re missing: the communal ritual of it all, as opposed to the social isolation of doing everything alone.

Every time I’m face-to-screen — scrolling through throwback holiday TikToks in a quiet room — I understand why those videos feel so nostalgic; they actually give me a pit in my stomach.

Our local mall is still open, technically, though I’m not sure anyone has actually been inside since 2016. These days, we shop online. We click, our orders show up at the door, and we call it a night. I go to bed at 10 p.m. on Thanksgiving, scrolling through deals with eye patches on and moisturizer slathered across my face, all from the warmth of my own bed.

And while I love romanticizing the past (typical!), the reality is that my nervous system probably needs this peace. We haven’t actually lost the best perks of Black Friday. You can get an engraved piece or custom monogrammed makeup pouch at an even steeper discount now — and without the physical toll. There’s no pressure from a doorbuster, no stranger trying to steal that thing you didn’t really need, and no glowing sign screaming at you to buy something right this second.

I’ll always miss the chaos of “the one place to be.” Still, after years of fighting through food courts, finally getting to pause feels like its own kind of holiday magic — and honestly, I’m pretty thankful for that.

item.title: 18 Cool Gifts That Are 10x More Impressive Than What You Usually Give
item.description: Want to give a gift that gets a "wow"? These ideas are way more impressive than what you're used to.
item.dc:creator: Anna Anderson
item.content:encoded:
Coming up with original gift ideas during the holidays can feel like a full-time job, especially if you’ve run through every iteration of scarf, sweater, and candle. Thankfully, gifts that make a splash are out there waiting for you — you just have to know where to look. This list is packed with cool gifts that provide plenty of wow factor, so you’ll be just as jazzed to wrap them up as your recipient will be to tear into them. So if you’re in a shopping rut, scroll on for some slam-dunk ideas that are way more impressive than what you’re used to.

A Smokeless Tabletop Fire Pit For Long, Lingering Evenings Outside

Solo Stove Mesa Tabletop Fire Pit

For a gift that’s cozy, festive, and impressive all at once, the Solo Stove Mesa tabletop fire pit delivers. It’s versatile for just about anyone on your list: Entertainers will love it for patio dinner parties, homebodies will appreciate snuggling up with a book next to it, and campers will look forward to toting it along on their next wilderness adventure. The smokeless design eliminates the number-one annoyance of traditional wood-burning fires and the stainless steel construction isn’t just sleek and modern — it’s also designed to stand up to years of enjoyment. The Mesa XL weighs just 2.3 pounds and takes up just 7 inches of surface space, and you can opt for a smaller version if you prefer something even more compact.

A Top-Grain Italian Leather Toiletry Bag With Separated Compartments

Quince Italian Leather Dual Compartment Toiletry Bag

Traveling feels a bit more luxe when your toothpaste and comb live inside this dual-compartment toiletry bag. The bag has a high-end look and feel, thanks to the top-grain Italian leather construction that’s available in rich shades like cognac, garnet red, taupe, and navy. (The leather is sourced from a tannery certified for using sustainable practices, so it’s a buy you can feel good about, too.) The spacious top compartment opens wide for easy viewing, eliminating the frustration of digging around and searching, while the bottom compartment unzips to reveal storage for smaller items as well as straps for a toothbrush, razor, or makeup brushes. It’s a thoughtful gift for frequent travelers or anyone looking forward to an upcoming trip.

A Sophisticated Smart Clock That Will Give Their Sleep Routine A Glow Up

Hatch Sleep Clock

For anyone who takes their sleep seriously or is ready to start, the Hatch sleep clock will be a true game changer. Don’t be fooled by its sleek, minimalist design; it’s packed with genuinely useful features that can change their sleep for the better, like a library of soothing sleep sounds to help them dose off, a customizable sun-rise alarm clock to gently wake them up, a bedside light in an assortment of colors, and a dimmable interface for the light-sensitive sleeper. While it works with a companion app, it can also be controlled with the simple button interface so they can stay off their phone before bedtime. Even better: Right now it’s 25% off as part of Hatch’s early Black Friday sale.

Luxurious Suede Slippers From A Cult-Favorite Brand

Psycho Bunny Suede Slippers

Handsome cow suede outers meet genuine shearling inners with these decadent slippers. The sophisticated lounge shoes come in tan or dark brown hues, both with the distinct Psycho Bunny logo stitched across the uppers in a slightly contrasting thread for a subtle embellishment that makes these look just as good as they feel.

A Plush Blanket & Comforter Set That’s Cozier Than You Can Imagine

Bedsure 2-in-1 Comforter Set (6 Pieces)

Cozying up for a long winter’s nap is a lot more tempting when you gift this two-in-one comforter set. It comes with a soft, prewashed comforter paired with a plush faux fur blanket — use them separately or snap them together to create a double-layer of comfort. Pillowcases and plush shams are included, too, so you can pretty much transform your bed setup into a cloud-like haven. It comes in sizes from twin to oversized king and the color selection makes it easy to find an aesthetic match.

A Hand-Painted Ceramic Bowl That’ll Make Even Soup & Cereal Feel Special

ALMA Hand-Painted Microwavable Soup Bowl with Loop Handle 18.6oz, Cereal Bowl With Handle Great for Berry, Fruits, Chili, Stew, Ice cream,Floral Soup Mug for Women

Amazon -

If you love a practical gift that still feels special, this hand-painted ceramic soup bowl is a beautiful option that’s guaranteed to get use. The oversized loop handle makes it easy to carry from the kitchen to the couch, and the dishwasher- and microwave-safe material means your recipient won’t have to think twice about heating up a bowl of tomato soup. It comes in more than a dozen colorful, floral designs, all with a wavy rim for a unique, boutique-worthy design touch.

A Lamp With A Levitating Light Bulb That Feels Like Magic

VGAzer Magnetic Levitating Light Bulb Lamp

You don’t have to be a kid to appreciate a little magic. This lamp uses the power of magnets to make the light bulb float and spin (nope, it’s not just an optical illusion), creating a mesmerizing effect on desktops and side tables. The energy-efficient LED bulb is designed to last up to 50,000 hours and features a visible filament for a vintage-inspired look and a warm, cozy glow. If you’re shopping for someone who loves an out-of-the-ordinary gift, this is sure to please.

A Cookie Subscription Box For Anyone Who Appreciates The Sweeter Things In Life

Goldbelly Monthly Cookie Subscription

Who wouldn’t want a box of cookies to show up on their doorstep once a month? Instead of you having to bake a batch and trudge to the post office, Goldbelly will do it for you, providing enough treats for six to eight people each month. Each delivery features a different selection, from traditional cookies you might spot in an Italian bakery to colorful sprinkled cookies that look like a mini celebration. And since the batch shows up in a cute tin or box, each month feels like opening a new present. You can choose from subscriptions that range from three months to indefinitely, making it easy to stay within your budget preferences.

A Classic Nylon Weekender With Luxury Vibes At A Lower Price Point

Quince Voyage Nylon Dual Compartment Weekender

The jet-setter in your life will get lots of use from this nylon weekender from Quince, a brand known for luxury-grade products at friendlier price points. The bag is a well-designed travel companion with a wide-opening main compartment that makes it easy to spot what you need, two strap options (handles and crossbody), and a padded laptop compartment that handles devices up to 13 inches. Even better, the zippered bottom compartment gives you a place to stash your shoes where the soles won’t get on your clean clothes. And it’s built for longevity: The water-repellent nylon stands up to surprise storms and the metal feet elevate the bag off the ground.

A Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard For The Person Who’s Always On The Go

Samsers Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard with Touchpad

If you know someone who travels for work, takes full advantage of their remote job, or simply writes a tome every time they send a text, this foldable Bluetooth keyboard will be a hit. The 6-ounce keyboard folds up to a mere 4 by 6 inches, making it easy to slip in a purse or tote, then folds out to a full 12 inches for easy typing. The included touch pad lets you do away with an extra mouse and the rechargeable battery lasts for up to 48 hours. It’s widely compatible (phones, tablets, laptops of any sort) and the color selection feels a lot more interesting than just choosing between standard black and gray.

A Shower Lamp That Adds Major Relaxation To Daily Routines

EZVALO Shower Lamp

Don’t underestimate the power of adding some mood lighting to your shower; it can make an ordinary task feel a lot more like a relaxing moment to pause. The IP65 construction is designed to stand up to steam and splashes, so you can set it on a shower shelf, the ledge of the tub, or just the bathroom counter. The lamp gives off a soft glow that’s much more gentle than the overhead light and the accompanying remote lets you toggle between colors if you’re in the market for something beyond standard warm white. Since your recipient probably showers, why not make the experience a little better?

A Tailgating Table That Turns Pre-Game Hangs & Camping Into A Party

Camerons All-In-One Tailgating Table

Whether it’s an NFL game, Little League, or just a weekend in the woods, this tailgating table will keep the snacks and drinks at the ready. When set up, it features four cupholders, an insulated cooler at the base, and a mesh basket that holds a bowl of snacks (chips, anyone?). It collapses easily and can be stored in the included carrying case — throw the strap over your shoulder if it’s a hike between your car and the designated hangout zone.

A Cult-Favorite Apron Worn By High-End Chefs

Hedley & Bennett Crossback Apron

If you have a home cook, baker, or grill master in your life, a quality apron is an amazing way to let them know you see their skill (and appreciate it). The cult-favorite apron from Hedley & Bennett has been worn by high-end chefs like Nancy Silverton and Top Chef winner Richard Blais, making it a truly special gift for anyone who spends time in the kitchen. The cross-back straps are designed to distribute pressure and go easy on your neck, making it wearable for long kitchen sessions, and the pockets are perfect for meat thermometers, cooking tools, and (of course) your phone. Choose from multiple colors and denim washes.

A Cozy, Puffy Outdoor Blanket From Rumpl

Rumpl Original Puffy Blanket

Give the gift of warmth, whether your recipient is a camper, football fan, or someone who just appreciates hanging out in the backyard no matter the season. The Rumpl puffy blanket offers a layer of insulated warmth courtesy of post-consumer recycled materials. It’s water resistant and machine washable, so getting caught in the rain and coffee spills are no big deal. Paracord corner staking loops keep it secure in wind and the cape clip lets you wear it around your shoulders hands free. It comes in solids as well as designs inspired by national parks, sunsets, and landscape scenes.

A Honey-Infused Hair Perfume That Adds Shine With Every Spritz

Gisou Honey Infused Hair Perfume

Perfume is a classic gift for a reason, but this perfume for hair feels a lot more original. Infused with honey, it actually nourishes hair as it fragrances it, softening strands and adding shine. The light mist helps it distribute evenly, so it won’t cling to just one spot and weigh hair down. Perfect for beauty obsessives and those who wouldn’t mind adding something unique to their fragrance collection, it comes in three floral-forward scents.

A Therapeutic Eye Mask With Massage, Heat, & Compression

Therabody SmartGoggles

The SmartGoggles from Therabody are self care taken to the next level. With a 100% blackout design, the goggles offer compression, massage, and heat therapy for a full sensory experience, making them the perfect gift for anyone in need of a little relaxation (or in need of relief from frequent headaches). Each session is customized to you; the goggles boast a biometric sensor that measures your heart rate, then vibrates at a lower frequency to help create a sense of calm.

A Water Droplet-Shaped Weather Glass With Crystals That Change With The Atmosphere

Uncommon Goods Weather Changing Water Droplet

If you know someone who obsessively checks their weather app (or someone who just loves conversation-starting decor), this storm glass will be a gift that provides endless fascination. Shaped like a water droplet, the interior creates crystal formations that shape-shift with atmospheric changes. Want to download a little history with your gift? Storm glasses like this were used by navigators dating back to the 19th century (although you’d have been hard-pressed to find one that looks this cool).

A Salt & Stone Body Wash Discovery Set With Delicious Scents

Salt & Stone Body Wash Discovery Set

This body wash discovery set from Salt & Stone feels luxe (beautiful scents, aesthetic packaging), but is all but guaranteed to be used, making it a special gift you know won’t go to waste. The set includes four earthy scents, like saffron and cedar and santal and vetiver, transforming any standard shower into an aromatic relaxation session. The body wash itself is a gel formula infused with brightening vitamin C and hydrating hyaluronic acid, leaving skin soft and smooth.

An Airy Cotton Robe That Makes Every Morning Feel Spa-Like

Quince Soft Layered Turkish Cotton Robe

This cotton robe from Quince is an elevated staple that’s cozy enough for winter but lightweight enough to keep wearing through the summer. It’s made from prewashed long-staple Turkish cotton, all in four layers for an airy, cloud-like feel. The shawl collar and tie closure keep the look classic, while the oversized patch pockets are perfect for stashing your phone when you step out to get the mail. The soft color options give it a spa feel, making it a truly impressive gift option.

A Splurge-Worthy Set Of Plush Organic Cotton Towels

Coyuchi Cloud Loom Organic Towels (6-Piece Set)

There are towels and then there are towels and Coyuchi’s Cloud Loom organic towels fall into the latter category. They’re perfect for anyone who loves the finer things in life or anyone who just sees the sense in spending a little extra for something you do every day (shower and wash your face). Voted the “Best Splurge Towels” by Oprah Daily, they’re made from long-staple Turkish cotton and boast a plush, fluffy texture that feels heavenly against the skin. They’re weighty and feel luxe, making them genuinely impressive to unwrap.

item.title: The Best Gifts For Manicure Lovers, According To Nail Artists
item.description: The best nail gifts of 2027 for manicure enthusiasts, according to top nail artists — from cuticle treatments to hand creams, press-ons, and more.
item.dc:creator: Iman Balagam
item.content:encoded:
Gift-giving can be stressful, especially when your loved ones aren’t exactly sending you neatly organized wish lists divided by price point (my sisters). Thankfully, shopping for someone with a particular passion — like nails — can make things a little easier.

Whether they’re curing their own nails at home with a UV lamp, recreating Hailey Bieber’s latest mani design at the salon every two weeks, or spending a small fortune on nail art without batting an eye, there’s no shortage of options for these friends. Because even the smallest upgrades to their nail routine can feel like a major treat.

To help narrow things down, Bustle polled top manicurists for their favorite nail-centric products to gift. Think reparative treatments for the friend who’s trying to recover from years of biting their nails, cuticle oils that won’t leave their fingers feeling greasy, and hand creams they’ll want to proudly display on their nightstand. And, of course, you can’t go wrong with gifting a new polish shade for their collection.

Below are the best gifts your mani-obsessed loved ones will actually be excited to unwrap.

For Buttery-Soft Hands

L'Occitane Nourishing & Protective Shea Butter Hand Cream

Sephora -

A hand cream is always a safe bet, particularly during the colder months. Manicurist Vikki Swan recommends this L’Occitane formula, which contains 20% shea butter to nourish dry skin. “It’s a luxurious yet practical gift that complements any manicure routine,” she says.

For The Mani Minimalist

Manucurist Active Glow Raspberry Nourishing Treatment Nail Polish

Sephora -

For the friend who prefers the naked nail look, Swan adores this nourishing polish from Manucurist. “I love how this treatment combines nail care with a beautiful, translucent pink tint and glossy finish,” she says. Designed to nourish and strengthen natural nails, it can be used on both fingers and toes without a base coat, top coat, or UV/LED lamp.

For The Seasonal Nail Enthusiast

Gelcare Margaux Red Gel Nail Polish

Revolve -

If you’re shopping for someone who swears by a classic holiday manicure, manicurist Viktoriia Voloshyna loves this rich burgundy shade from Gelcare. She calls it her “go-to winter red,” noting that it looks polished on almost every skin tone. “It works for any style, from short natural nails to long ones, and it looks elegant on its own without any nail art,” she says.

The Handbag Hydration Hero

Essie On A Roll Apricot Cuticle Oil

Ulta -

Cuticle oil is one of those little luxuries your nail-obsessed friend will actually use. Manicurist Elle Gerstein calls this Essie option the perfect stocking stuffer. “I always tell my clients that cuticle oil is a daily essential, especially during the winter,” she says. “I love the roller applicator because you can keep it in your handbag and use it throughout the day.”

For The Friend Who Loves Options

Soiree Mini Flight

Dazzle Dry -

Gerstein is also a fan of Dazzle Dry’s mini polish collections, particularly this festive set. “The colors are sophisticated, festive, and a little edgy,” she says. “I love gifting mini collections because they encourage people to experiment with colors they might not normally gravitate toward without committing to a full-size bottle.”

A Little Pedi Pick-Me-Up

Gelcare Pedicure Kit

Revolve -

Cold-weather feet deserve a little TLC, too. Manicurist Olivia de Montagnac swears by this pedicure kit, which includes everything you need for at-home foot maintenance. “We are not neglecting our feet this winter,” she says. “The callus remover is my all-time favorite, and I like that the exfoliating pads are disposable.”

A Trio Of Crowd-Pleasers

The Holiday Trio

Celisse -

De Montagnac also recommends this holiday trio from Celisse, featuring three shades that are basically guaranteed to earn a spot in anyone’s polish rotation. “Everything from Celisse is thoughtfully designed and curated,” she says. And the velvet packaging is just one more reason it deserves a spot under the tree.

This Whole-Body Treat

Summer Fridays Body Butter Balm Pistachio Milk

Sephora -

For a gift that goes beyond the usual nail-care staples, de Montagnac recommends this buttery balm from Summer Fridays. The luxe formula delivers a hefty dose of hydration anywhere from hands to heels. “I use it on my hands, but I also love using it on my legs and feet for a massage,” she says. “Vanilla smells amazing, but Pistachio is my favorite!”

A Sanitizer Glow-Up

Gemi Hand Sanitizer + Serum Set

Amazon -

Hand sanitizer may not scream exciting gift, but this set makes the everyday essential feel a little more luxe. Manicurist Marisa Carmichael loves the formulas, which cleanse while keeping hands moisturized. “These are my favorite sanitizers. The scents are gorgeous and not overpowering, and they have a moisturizing serum that leaves hands soft and clean.” Think of it as K-beauty for your hands.

A Five-Star Cuticle Treatment

Nourish Cuticle Cream

Shige Beauty -

If your friend likes her nail care with a side of luxury, Carmichael recommends this cuticle cream. “It feels so elegant and has a really fresh scent,” she says. She's also a fan of its hydrating formula, which nourishes cuticles without leaving behind a greasy residue.

For Nails In Their Recovery Era

ePhD Bond Repair Nail Treatment

Epres -

For the friend whose nails have seen better days, Carmichael recommends this bond-repair treatment. “It’s a liquid that penetrates the nail plate and bonds to make nails stronger,” she explains. Even better, it can be worn underneath nail polish, so they don't have to sacrifice their regular mani routine while nursing their nails back to health.

For A Head-To-Toe Glow

NUXE Huile Prodigieuse Florale Dry Body Oil

Amazon -

A good body oil is always appreciated, and manicurist Marielle Co says this one is a standout. “Every time I’ve used this product on a client, they rave about it,” she says. “Not only does it smell amazing, but it leaves the skin with a beautiful glow without feeling greasy. It is so nourishing and hydrating. I love that it can be used all over the body, especially on the hands and cuticles.”

For The Nail-Care Overachiever

OPI Repair Mode Bond Building Nail Serum

Amazon -

Some manicure devotees take their nail health routine very seriously. For these friends, Co recommends adding a strengthening treatment to the mix. “Our nails rely on keratin, so keeping them strong and hydrated is key,” she says. “I always tell my clients that nail health starts with taking care of the natural nail underneath the polish. Strengthening treatments can help improve resilience and reduce breakage — especially if you're trying to avoid those dreaded broken nails.”

A Paris Fashion Week-Approved Mani

Manucurist Active Routine Gift Set

Amazon -

Co first discovered Manucurist backstage at Paris Fashion Week and has been a fan ever since. Known for its vegan, plant-based formulas and more conscious approach to nail care, the brand makes some of her favorite manicure essentials. “I love having a few clean, easy-to-use essentials on hand, and this kit covers three things I think are important: hydration, color, and overall nail health,” she says. “It’s perfect for someone who loves keeping their nails looking polished while still prioritizing the health of their natural nails.”

For The Nail Art Chameleon

BTArtbox Press On Nails

Amazon -

Press-on nails are the ultimate gift for the friend who's rocking a different design every time you see them. Co loves this brand for its range of options across skin tones, shapes, lengths, and designs. “It’s a great way to experiment with different nail looks without committing to a salon appointment,” she says. “There's something for just about everyone's personal style.”

A Personalized Mani Upgrade

The Cuticle Pen

HEIRÉE -

Manicurist Sonya Belakhlef loves this cuticle pen for its luxe feel and customizable, monogrammed pouch. It's also at the top of their own holiday shopping list. “I personally am gifting my clients these pens this year!”

The Unexpected Nail-Care Essential

Treatment-Boosting Gloves

Habelo -

For the friend who spends a lot of time behind the wheel, Belakhlef recommends these treatment-boosting gloves. They're a thoughtful alternative to yet another bottle of nail polish — especially for someone whose collection is already overflowing. “I love using these gloves in the car for sun protection,” they say.

The Ultimate Hand-Care Splurge

Omnilux Contour Glove with Red and Near Infrared Light Therapy LED Device

Sephora -

If they aren’t messing around with their hand care routine, Belakhlef suggests going all out with this red and near-infrared light therapy glove. Think of it as the gift of 10 minutes of mandatory, phone-free self-care.

A Hand-Hydrating MVP

Sidia Soaked: The Hand Serum

Revolve -

A good hand serum should feel as lovely as it works. Belakhlef recommends Sidia for its beautiful scents and textures, and particularly enjoys incorporating its serum into their routine.

A Portable Nail Booster

Tenoverten The Rose Oil

Ulta -

Cuticle oil might seem like a simple gift, but it's one they'll actually put to use. Manicurist Sandra Wei recommends looking for a formula with nourishing ingredients like jojoba oil and vitamin E to help ward off dryness and hangnails. “It’s especially beneficial for those who regularly get gel manicures, as daily cuticle care helps keep the skin surrounding the nails soft and well-maintained,” she says.

Beauty Sleep For Your Hands

Paume Hand & Foot Recovery Set

Ulta -

For a more indulgent at-home treatment, Wei recommends overnight moisturizing gloves. “I recommend applying a nourishing hand cream and cuticle oil before putting on soft cotton gloves at bedtime to help retain moisture and keep the skin around the nails soft and hydrated,” she says. It's a simple way to turn an everyday hand-care routine into a relaxing at-home spa ritual.

The Good-Hands Guarantee

Diptyque Luxurious Hand Balm

Nordstrom -

Wei is also a big believer in keeping a good hand cream within reach, especially during the colder months. She recommends looking for formulas with moisturizing ingredients like shea butter, glycerin, or ceramides to help protect against seasonal dryness. “This is especially important during the colder months, when the skin around the nails tends to become dry and rough. A good hand cream makes a wonderful holiday gift because it encourages a convenient moment of everyday self-care.”

item.title: Spicy Holiday Romance Books That Are Perfect For Christmas
item.description: Feeling festive... and flirty? Here are five steamy holiday romance books that pair Christmas settings with glorious, gift-wrapped spice.
item.dc:creator: Grace Wehniainen
item.content:encoded:
Winter may be upon us, but the holidays have always brought a kind of heat (and not just from the fireplace). Whether it’s the winky banter of “Baby It’s Cold Outside” or the irresistible chemistry of The Holiday, some of the season’s most beloved pop culture is about getting a little flirty. And why not?

If you’re dreaming of a steamy romance set at Christmastime, options abound — and there’s no better time of year to curl up with a good book. From festive getaways to a passionate encounter with a figure from Yuletide folklore, here are five spicy holiday romance books to gift yourself this season.

Window Shopping by Tessa Bailey

Trying to move on from a rocky past, Stella finds work designing the holiday window display for a New York City department store. Complicating her fresh start is a sizzling crush on her new boss, Aiden, who will do just about anything to make her happy.

Royal Holiday by Jasmine Guillory

Along for her daughter’s work trip in London, Vivian discovers a surprising connection with royal secretary Malcolm, forcing them to consider whether their festive fling has staying power beyond the holidays.

What’s a Girl Gotta Do to Get on the Naughty List? by Kimberly Lemming

Prefer your holiday spice with a side of cheeky romantasy? This novella follows Daphne, a woman who embarks on a steamy fling with Krampus — as in, the horned Christmas demon — when he tracks her down from his naughty list one Christmas Eve.

Kiss Her Once for Me by Alison Cochrun

A year after meeting her dream girl turned sour, Ellie agrees to a marriage of convenience with her work landlord Andrew in this story partially inspired by While You Were Sleeping. When trying to sell their romance to his family over Christmas, Ellie learns that her long-lost fling is Andrew’s sister, Jack, for whom she still has some very real, complicated feelings.

A Novel Christmas by Charity Shané

In this delightful holiday rom-com about writing holiday rom-coms, novelist Saira retreats to a festive small town to research for her next novel. Though she’s not exactly thrilled by her publisher’s assignment, Saira finds unexpected inspiration in her new neighbor, Dorian, a volunteer firefighter who sets her heart ablaze.

item.title: Ally Financial Took Over The NWSL Championship At Ally House
item.description: The activation featured exclusive merch, live shows, and special appearances from stars like Brandi Chastain, Briana Scurry, and Paige Bueckers.
item.dc:creator: Megan LaCreta
item.content:encoded:
As the saying goes, everyone watches women’s sports — and that’s thanks, in part, to Ally Financial. In 2022, the virtual bank collaborated with CBS to move the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) Finals to primetime for the first time ever — a slot it has kept ever since, including during Saturday night’s championship match-up between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current.

With efforts led by Ally CMO and former Michigan State soccer player Andrea Brimmer, the bank has been one of the leading forces championing the NWSL. This April, Ally achieved its groundbreaking 50/50 media pledge, devoting equal advertising spending toward men's and women's sports media. This past week, as the teams geared up for the championship game, Ally House, the bank’s fan activation, provided a space for soccer superfans and NWSL icons to come together in celebration of the sport they love.

The Brains Behind Ally House

When Ally first entered their partnership with the NWSL in 2021, far fewer eyes were on women’s soccer.

“My first championship game in Louisville, it was noon on a Saturday, and it just felt like going to a high school soccer game,” Brimmer says. “We came out of that and said, ‘We’ve got to make this something.’”

That experience informed Ally’s push to get the Finals moved to primetime television, and also to create an activation and fandom space in Ally House.

“This is the soccer Super Bowl, and if you go to the Super Bowl for the NFL, you see these kind of activations everywhere,” Brimmer says. “We wanted to bring that kind of gravitas to women's soccer.”

Ally House Was The Place To Be At The NWSL Finals

Brimmer’s dream was certainly realized. The activation, held on Nov. 20 and 21, took place at the NWSL Championship Ally House, just minutes from the match at Audi Stadium in Washington, D.C. The space was filled with fans of all ages — from adult fans sipping on drinks from the bar, to teenage boys to infant girls being pushed by their parents in a stroller.

The event included a custom charm bar, plus passed appetizers like sliders and pigs-in-a-blanket. While the DJ played, fans grabbed exclusive merch from Ally, sodas and beers from the bar, and sipped on matchas and lattes from Pitchside Coffee, a Kansas City-based coffee shop co-owned by six current and former NWSL players: Elizabeth Ball, Vanessa DiBernardo, Kristen Hamilton, Hailie Mace, Desiree Scott, and Mallory Weber.

Appearances From Superstar Guests

The main event on Friday was a live episode of The RE-CAP Show with former NWSL stars Tobin Heath and Christen Press, along with special guests, former players Merritt Mathias and Briana Scurry, and Guerilla FC organizers Chris Bowerbank and Elisa Davidson. The energy in the room was electric — even though it was largely filled with enthusiastic Spirit fans, the entire space filled with applause and shouts of approval when Heath brough up Kansas City devoting resources to building the first-ever purpose-built stadium for a professional women's sports team.

The highlight of Saturday was another live show, this time, an episode of Welcome To The Party with former NWSL players Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. The players first brought out Brimmer and Danette Leighton, CEO of the Women’s Sports Foundation, to discuss the importance of Title IX in women’s sports. Then, they welcomed a panel of surprise guests to the stage: WNBA star Paige Bueckers, Claire Hutton of Bay FC, and NWSL legend Brandi Chastain. They played a game, pitting “youngins” Bueckers and Hutton against ‘99ers Foudy and Chastain.

The game, kicking balls into a laundry basket, ended in a tie when nobody bothered to keep count. The competitive spirit at Audi Stadium was at an all-time high — whereas at Ally House, people simply gathered to have a good time.

item.title: Nordstrom's New David Bowie Collab Is Full Of Cool-Girl Holiday Gifts
item.description: Nordstrom just dropped Bowie80, a David Bowie holiday collection and pop-up featuring Susan Alexandra, Kim Shui, and Marc Jacobs. Shop our top picks.
item.dc:creator: Megan LaCreta
item.content:encoded:
Your holiday shopping list just got a major glam-rock upgrade. Ahead of what would have been David Bowie’s 80th birthday, Nordstrom teamed up with the late icon’s estate for an exclusive designer collab and immersive pop-ups in New York, Chicago, and Seattle that celebrate his lasting influence on music and fashion.

Available in stores and online through Jan. 8 (his birthday), Bowie80 is for anyone who believes band merch can heal society — and also wants a designer handbag to match. Whether you’re browsing the collection, wandering through the interactive exhibits, or watching “Let’s Dance” (Nordstrom’s short hero film set to Bowie’s track of the same name), there’s plenty here to grab for your most stylish friend — or add to your own wish list.

Step Inside The Bowie80 Pop-Ups

If you live near one of Nordstrom’s three flagship locations, the pop-up is worth a trip in person. Each exhibit features larger-than-life archival photos of Bowie across all of his eras, rare vinyl and albums on display, and an interactive phone booth where you can actually listen to messages from the artist himself.

In New York City, an interactive tap-and-explore wall lets you experience Bowie’s iconic career hands-on.

The Collab Roster Does Not Miss

The real draw, though, is the stacked lineup of indie darlings and luxury heavyweights who contributed to the drop. Marc Jacobs — who custom-designed Lady Gaga’s tribute to Bowie at the 2016 Grammy Awards — is on the roster, with select pieces debuting in the flagship pop-ups.

On the cool-girl fashion front, Kim Shui brought her signature edge with a lineup of bedazzled baby tees, while kitschy-chic labels Anya Hindmarch and Susan Alexandra took over the accessories with wallets, keychains, crossbodies, and Alexandra’s cult-favorite beaded bags.

Streetwear favorites also made an appearance. Japanese cult labels like Number (N)ine and UNDERCOVER are part of the broader collaboration — keep an eye out for their pieces in flagship stores or upcoming online drops — while PLEASURES already has graphic tees and hoodies ready to shop now.

Add These Pieces To Your Wish List

Whether you’re treating yourself or shopping for the biggest Bowie stan in your group chat, shop our favorite picks from the collection below (and check out the full drop in stores and on Nordstrom’s site).

item.title: Lea Michele’s Beauty Routine Includes Red Lights & Kiehl’s Body Butter
item.description: Lea Michele on her Kiehl’s campaign, beauty routine, self-care rituals, and everyday makeup essentials.
item.dc:creator: Leigh Scheps
item.content:encoded:
Lea Michele is rethinking wellness. “I just saw this interview that Alanis Morissette did, and she said she doesn’t believe in wellness — she believes in wholeness. And I really love that concept now,” she tells me over Zoom. “Wholeness has always been something that I make a priority, and it helps me be a better wife, mother, and performer.”

It’s a philosophy that makes sense for someone whose recent schedule has included a sold-out concert at New York’s Beacon Theater with former Chess costar Aaron Tveit, a guest-starring role on CBS’ Elsbeth, and a new holiday campaign with Kiehl’s. The morning after the concert, Michele was still riding high. “It really was such an epic day,” she says. “I think it was the first time I was returning to television in many years — maybe 10.”

Between late-night performances and morning school drop-offs, Michele prioritizes small moments of self-care. “I take care of my body and my voice in the same way that an athlete would if they were going to go and play a game,” she says.

Ahead, the Broadway star opens up about her postshow beauty routine, the makeup products she keeps in her purse, and the rituals that help her unwind.

What was your favorite moment from the concert?

I love watching Aaron perform. His rendition of “Without You” and “Glory” from Rent — I just fangirl out. I got to do “Nobody’s Side,” and I was flipping my hair around and rocking out with our amazing guitarist Aurélien [Budynek]. It’s obviously not stuff that you get to do onstage every night when you’re on Broadway.

What does your postshow self-care routine look like?

Number one, I always wash my face. Something I’m obsessed with is cleaning my cell phone and my sunglasses with alcohol at the end of the night. I take a nice shower. Last night, I made myself some sourdough toast, got into bed, checked a couple of text messages, took my little magnesium tea, and went to sleep.

After performing and spending hours in makeup, what are the little things you do to reset?

I think everything starts from within. It’s very hard to get good sleep with two children, but I really try to prioritize it. I have my Hatch light by my bedside, and it goes off at 9:30 p.m. with this warm red light and meditative music that reminds me it’s time to wind down.

I try to drink a ton of water and just take good care of myself. I sit and meditate on the floor in my closet with my red light. It’s one of my favorite little weird private habits.

I have so many wellness things in my house. I have my HigherDOSE [infrared sauna blanket] — I try to do that every day if I can.

What’s one beauty product you always have on you?

I’ve been a fan of Kiehl’s for so many years. I love their body moisturizer. It’s something that I always keep on me, even in my purse, to help my dry skin get through the horrible changing weather.

What does your makeup routine look like for school drop-offs or running around the neighborhood?

I’ll use a foundation, powder, a really nice cream blush, some mascara, a little eyebrow pencil, and some lip gloss. I like the brands Gucci Westman and Saie. I have one blush brush, and it makes getting ready so quick and so easy now.

What’s one beauty ritual that feels like a luxury to you that you do for yourself, not because you have an on-camera appearance or performance?

Getting a lymphatic massage is such a great reset. It’s something that I used to do only for red carpets, but now I do them for myself.

I also love a good bath. I go to Duane Reade, get a bag of Epsom salt, dump it in with a couple drops of lavender oil, and I feel like I’m at a spa. I light a little candle, pour myself a cup of tea, and it feels just as good as any luxury spa.

Last night, you sang “Move On” from Sunday in the Park With George and said it was “a look into the future.” What did you mean by that?

I think what I’ve learned over the past couple of years on Broadway is just how much my joy for what I do is growing and growing and growing. I might not have the opportunity now to play some of the younger ingenue roles, but I think that there are still so many amazing roles that are out there and in store for me. I can’t wait to play them all.

You could play The Nanny. Perfect role for you.

Oh my God, you’re not the first person to tell me that.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

item.title: The 2016 Thanksgiving Outfit Is The Nostalgic Look Of The Season
item.description: Looking back on the iconic black top, suede skirt, and thigh-high boots combo, a decade after its cultural peak.
item.dc:creator: Megan LaCreta
item.content:encoded:
Certain outfits are so iconic, I can close my eyes and picture them with ease. Utter the words “Marilyn Monroe dress,” and I’m automatically envisioning a white halter, plunging neckline, and billowy skirt. Say “Britney and Justin at the American Music Awards,” and I’ll have visions of Canadian tuxedos floating in my head. The same thing goes for the phrase “2016 Thanksgiving outfit.” Just three words, and I know exactly what you’re talking about.

If you’re not in the same boat, let me enlighten you. The recipe for a 2016 Thanksgiving outfit is simple: black top, corduroy or suede skirt, and black boots. The top is usually fitted, the skirt usually with a front button detail, and the boots usually above-the-knee. Some elements could be swapped in and out depending on your preference — add a chunky cardigan or tights for some warmth, or a giant “Christian Girl Autumn”-esque hat for a touch of seasonal pizzazz. Because it was 2016, the look was usually accompanied by a matte lip courtesy of Kylie Cosmetics and blocky eyebrows courtesy of Anastasia Beverly Hills. Maybe an Urban Decay smoky eye was thrown into the mix, if that was your journey. But the basic formula was always the same.

Over time, the distinct outfit has largely faded from holiday Instagram feeds. But in the decade that has passed since the Thanksgiving outfit was at its cultural peak, no clothing successor has managed to become synonymous with the holiday’s aesthetic quite like this one. I’m not suggesting that anyone celebrate the look’s anniversary with a revival — it might be a few more years before the trend cycle allows it to feel like anything other than OG YouTuber cosplay — but in the spirit of gratitude, I’d like to honor its legacy. Allow me to give thanks to the Thanksgiving outfit.

In Loving Memory Of An Iconic OOTD

The black-top/button-skirt/tall-boot combo is such an iconic look, I was certain there would be some celeb examples. But in my search for photos, I kept coming up empty. Fortunately, plenty of examples of the exact outfit formula, down to a T, can be found on TikTok.

The outfit speaks to a certain 2010s nostalgia. For millennials and elder Gen Z, the ’fit harkens to memories of high school, college, or young adulthood. A time soundtracked by Drake and Fetty Wap, when the Clarendon and dog filter dominated Instagram posts and Snapchat streaks were a form of social currency.

Plenty of videos and comments joke about wearing the getup, coupled with a burgundy cut-crease eye look, just to sit on a relative’s couch for a few hours while your extended family argues politics over the turkey. “I remember taking it VERY serious. Spent 2-3hrs getting ready to sit down, eat, and nap,” user @justforthejc commented on one TikTok reminiscing on the look. The contrast in the outfit’s formality to the vibe of chilling in the living room strikes the same chord as the iconic, and widely memed, Ariel Winter Modern Family press event look. Yes, you’re overdressed… but what a serve!

The 2016 Thanksgiving Outfit & Me

You might be shocked to find out, despite being able to wax poetic about the Thanksgiving outfit of 2016, that I never actually wore it myself. My truth: Despite being in high school at the height of the craze, I’ve always been a sweater and jeans girl on Thanksgiving.

I wish I rocked the thigh-highs on Turkey Day at least once, though. Having never participated in the trend when it was in, I feel like I missed out on an important cultural moment. Imagine living through the ’80s with no perm to show for it, or the 2020s having never made a TikTok to “Renegade,” even if the video stayed in your drafts. When I scroll upon a post looking back on the tried and true outfit formula, I feel a nostalgia for something I never experienced.

At this point, I would label the trend expired, at least until the 2010s fashion revival hits and we’re all wearing patterned skinny jeans and chevrons in the spring again. It’s too late for me to truly experience the magic of sending Snap streaks in my black fitted bodysuit and suede mini skirt during its heyday. That FOMO is strong as I pack my bags to head home for the holiday — checking the weather and texting my mom to ask what our plans are as I attempt to piece together a decent look. If only I had a surefire uniform at the ready.

item.title: 10 Best Books By Indigenous Authors From The Past 10 Years
item.description: A roundup of books by Indigenous authors that center Native culture and history.
item.dc:creator: Sophie Fishman
item.content:encoded:
The 21st century has been described by some as a renaissance for Native American fiction. Tommy Orange’s 2018 novel There There paved the way for a much-needed boom in the genre, with exciting new Indigenous voices finally stepping into the spotlight.

Literary fiction by Indigenous authors has seen a particularly meteoric rise. In 2021, Louise Erdrich won the Pulitzer Prize for The Night Watchman, a historic fiction set in 1953 North Dakota, based on her own Ojibwe grandfather’s life. Small Ceremonies, Kyle Edwards’ 2025 novel following a group of Indigenous teenagers and their community in Winnipeg, also made a splash.

There have also been must-reads in other genres. Deborah Jackson Taffa’s memoir Whiskey Tender, a finalist for the 2024 National Book Award, is a propulsive coming-of-age account intertwined with Native history.

Here are 10 books from the past decade to enjoy during Indigenous Heritage Month and beyond.

The Berry Pickers by Amanda Peters

In July 1962, a Mi’Kmaq family from Nova Scotia family travels to Maine to pick blueberries for the summer, but soon after, 4-year-old Ruthie goes missing. Meanwhile, Norma, the only child of wealthy overprotective parents in a nearby suburb, has always felt something about her life was amiss. Haunted by visions, Norma begins to realize her family has been keeping secrets from her, and spends decades trying to uncover the truth on a journey that ties her story to Ruthie’s.

Firekeeper's Daughter by Angeline Boulley

For years, 18-year-old Daunis has been dreaming of leaving her Michigan hometown and the nearby Ojibwe reservation for college. When a sudden tragedy strikes, however, Daunis instead finds herself as her mother’s caretaker. In the darkness of the moment, she meets Jamie, the star of her brother’s hockey team. Soon, though, the romance between the two will lead to tragedy, and Daunis is forced to go undercover for the FBI.

If the Dead Belong Here by Carson Faust

In Jordan, Wisconsin, 6-year-old Laurel Taylor is missing. As her family reels, her 14-year-old sister, Nadine, begins having nightmares that shake her foundation. Now convinced that Laurel’s disappearance is the result of past family tragedy, Nadine sets out in search of her sister.

Love Is a War Song by Danica Nava

After a national scandal, gossipy headlines and online threats drive pop singer Avery Fox from Hollywood to her grandmother’s ranch in rural Oklahoma. It’s there she meets ranch hand Lucas Iron Eyes, who, dedicated to preserving his Muscogee culture, is incredulous at what Avery represents; he sees her as an out-of-touch star disrespecting her own heritage. When Red Fox Ranch is in danger of shuttering, the two must strike up a deal to save it.

The Night Watchman by Louise Erdrich

In 1953 North Dakota, Thomas Wazhashk, a Chippewa Council member and the night watchman at a jewel bearing plant, learns about the “emancipation” bill about to hit the floor of the United States Congress. The bill is a threat to their way of life, challenging their sovereignty over their land and identity, so Thomas leads his community to fight it. Meanwhile, 19-year-old Pixie Paranteau is on her own journey. Her older sister, Vera, has disappeared to Minneapolis and is rumored to have a child. Saving every penny she can to find her, Patrice follows her sister’s footsteps to Minnesota where a world of violence awaits her.

The Seed Keeper by Diane Wilson

Rosalie Iron Wing grew up learning about the history of the Dakhóta people from her father, Ray. When he goes missing, Rosalie is sent to live with a nearby foster family. Years later, as a recently widowed mother, Rosalie returns to her former home in search of her past and the embrace of her community. As she grieves, Rosalie learns about the Iron Wing women who came before her and what it means to protect her tradition.

Small Ceremonies by Kyle Edwards

In Winnipeg’s North End, it might be the last ever high school hockey season for The Tigers. For players Tomahawk “Tommy” Shields and Clinton Whiteway, this means moving toward an uncertain future. Switching between perspectives, the novel traces the boys’ lives over the course of a year as they attempt to lead their team toward victory.

To the Moon and Back by Eliana Ramage

Growing up, Steph had one dream: to become the first Cherokee astronaut in space, even if it means leaving everyone and everything she’s ever known behind. In this debut novel, Eliana Ramage charts Steph’s journey from past to present, following her from Oklahoma to Connecticut to Hawaii to outer space.

Whiskey Tender by Deborah Jackson Taffa

The mixed granddaughter of Quechan Nation and Pueblo Tribe members, Deborah Jackson Taffa grew up in Navajo Territory in New Mexico, believing that achieving the “American Dream” was contingent on sacrificing her culture and customs. When she reaches adulthood, however, she begins to question that notion. A memoir shifting among the present, childhood memories, and decades of Native history, Whiskey Tender is a look at the stories America tells about itself.

White Horse by Erika T. Wurth

Kari James has spent her life trying to forget her mother who abandoned her at 2 years old. When her cousin Debby comes to town and gifts her a traditional bracelet, she begins to see horrifying visions of her mother and a mysterious creature. Unable to shake the images haunting her, Kari sets out in search of answers.

item.title: The Art Of Shopping Black Friday For Freakishly Good Gifts
item.description: Make the most of Black Friday and Cyber Monday with holiday gift-giving secrets from a celebrity concierge, a sommelier, and other elite year-round shoppers.
item.dc:creator: Lara Walsh
item.content:encoded:
Shopping for your loved ones can easily be the most stressful part of the holiday season. Maybe you’re stumped on what to get your longtime BFF, a new partner, or your well-intentioned mom who insists that she doesn’t need anything when you ask her to drop some hints before the Black Friday deals roll out. Suddenly, those same old candles or tired coffee mugs start looking dangerously tempting.

The problem? Generic or impersonal gifts are a guaranteed shortcut to closet clutter, and even a splurge-worthy trend doesn’t guarantee your recipient will actually love it. To help you level up your holiday shopping ahead of Cyber Week, we tapped the pros who’ve cracked the code on thoughtful presents — from a marketing manager raised by two generations of elite gift-givers to a celebrity concierge who shops for A-listers — to share their secrets for pulling off unforgettable finds.

Turn Your Notes App Into A Gifting Mastermind File

Bentley Boldt Hall, a New Orleans-based senior marketing manager at tasc Performance, learned from her grandmother Deede and mom Caroline to treat shopping for presents as “a year-round mindset” so she never lets the holidays “drive the rush.”

“If something strikes me in April that I know is perfect for someone on my list, I grab it [and] hide it,” she says. Her purchases live in a dedicated stash spot — a guest bedroom turned “costume closet/craft/gift room,” she admits, pointing out that living in New Orleans inherently demands costume storage — until she wraps them right before gifting.

To keep track of it all, she relies on her phone. “My inventory is tracked on a note on my phone, and I’ll highlight something in green when it’s been given,” she says. “Listen, because people often talk about what they want or need. I’ll text myself, jot down a note, or the best — create a calendar entry around the time I need to purchase the gift.”

That phone-first strategy inspired the present she’s most proud of: commissioned artwork for her bestie. After spotting her friend’s mom’s “beautiful vases” on the sweetheart table at her wedding, Boldt Hall turned the memory into a housewarming gift. “I snapped a photo of them on my phone and commissioned an artist, Tani Greenspan Koch, to paint prints of the vases for her new house. The art turned out beautifully and my friend absolutely loved them. I got to bring a memory from her wedding to her new life,” she says.

Upgrade Your Loved One’s Daily Habits

Márcio Jesus, a Brazil-based certified sommelier and maître d’ who writes gift guides on SommShelf, says those so-called “boring” gift ideas are often the ones your loved ones will actually reach for time and time again.

One easy approach is elevating something they already own — especially if you want to channel acts-of-service energy into solving a tiny daily headache. “The best gifts replace an object people own but would never upgrade themselves: a good waiter’s corkscrew instead of the cheap one in the drawer, two beautiful glasses instead of the mismatched set,” Jesus says. “People rarely buy themselves ‘better’ versions of everyday things.”

You can also take cues from the minor inconveniences your best friend or parent mentions in passing. “Notice their little frustrations: the leftover champagne that goes flat, the red wine drips on the tablecloth, the cork that always breaks,” he suggests. A quick search ahead of Black Friday can lead you to a clever fix they didn’t even know existed, all without breaking your budget.

Jesus’s golden rule for keeping your present out of a junk drawer? Make sure they can open and enjoy it immediately. “Make it ready to use tonight without another purchase,” he says. “Include what’s needed to enjoy the gift right away: the glasses with a bottle, the stopper with a sparkling wine.”

Craft An Experience Around A Shared Craving

A “self-proclaimed serial gifter” and “big foodie,” Hien Nguyen — the Australia-based founder of wellness brand Happy Way — says he tapped into his and his wife Lisa’s “weakness for pho” to create a memorable date-night experience.

“I was looking through my Notes app (where I keep little ideas about things Lisa has mentioned wanting to do and experiences we could enjoy together), I jotted down pho, and I came back to it a couple of days later,” he says. Brainstorming ways to turn their favorite dish into an interactive date led him to Vietnamese cooking workshops.

“Immediately, I thought it would be perfect,” he says. “Because even though we love the food so much and try to re-create it often, it’s very different when you’re learning the process of getting all those flavors and ingredients right.”

Use Next-Level Presentation To Create A “Wow Factor”

Brian Daniel, the founder of the Los Angeles-based Celebrity PA Network, shops for A-list clients and helps celebrity assistants buy presents for their famous bosses. He credits his “overactive imagination” and years of experience for taking his gift-giving skills to the next level, approaching every shopping trip with the same mindset: “How can I bring a ‘wow factor’ to the person who is going to open it?”

Gifts “don’t have to be expensive, but they do need to be thoughtful,” he says, recalling when one friend was brought to tears by the custom packaging he used to zhuzh up a kit of her favorite makeup.

“I put it in an amazing, handcrafted basket with excelsior (Aspen wood shavings made for packing luxe items) and had it delivered. She called me and left a message, and she was crying. She said, and I quote, ‘Brian, this is the most amazing and thoughtful gift anyone has ever given me. I’ll never forget you,’” he recalls. “Now, I should mention that she was married to a famous football player, and she was used to getting the finest and most expensive things in life. Yet my $300 gift totally blew her socks off.”

Match Your Gift To An Emotional Moment

Alyssa Ostroff, the Florida-based founder of Self-Care Shirts, believes the best gifts make the recipient feel seen. “For me, the gift has to meet the person exactly where they are emotionally, not just mark an occasion,” she says.

“When my sister moved to New York, I gave her a gift card loaded with a couple hundred dollars specifically for plane tickets, so that anytime she felt homesick, coming home was already paid for,” Ostroff shares. “The gift wasn’t money. It was permission to come home.”

Along those same lines, a great gift can also give someone “permission” to indulge in a little luxury. “The best presents are often the thing someone wants but won’t get for themselves — the rest, the small indulgence, the treat that feels frivolous,” she says. “Giving it removes their guilt, and that’s the actual gift.”

Separate Your Own Taste From The Equation

“My biggest rule: Never buy something just because you like it. It’s not about your taste; it’s about theirs,” Ostroff says. “Now, in my 30s, I mostly want experiences and memories — a play, a little weekend trip, an art exhibit — and I lean that way for others, too. But I’ve also learned not everyone is me. Some people treasure something physical they can wear or hold.”

To put that rule into practice — and resist her own bias toward experiences — she picked out microwavable lavender heating gloves, a cozy robe, and a neck wrap to ease her mother-in-law’s chronic pain while recovering from hand surgery. “It’s practical, soothing, and usable every day,” she says.

How To Nail The Holidays This Year

You don’t need an A-list budget or a celebrity concierge on speed dial to become a legendary gift-giver. The secret is simple: Pay attention.

As you map out your Black Friday shopping strategy this season, borrow a page from these pros — track the tiny details, solve an everyday annoyance, and don’t underestimate great presentation — to land on a gift your loved one will genuinely treasure long after the wrapping paper is gone.

item.title: 10 Years After The ‘Gilmore Girls’ Revival, The Winter ’Fits Still Hit
item.description: To mark 10 years of 'Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life', we're revisiting Lorelai and Rory's best winter outfits — from chunky beanies to sleek leather blazers.
item.dc:creator: Alyssa Lapid
item.content:encoded:
Lorelai and Rory Gilmore are the undisputed fall style icons. A vignette of the mother-daughter duo sipping coffee at Luke’s, dressed in leather blazers and preppy skirts, is practically an autumn postcard. But their winter ‘fits have flown relatively under the radar. And in this humble fashion girl’s opinion, they deserve just as much praise.

It wasn’t until Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life, the revival that landed on Netflix 10 years ago — opening right in the middle of a snowy winter — that I truly appreciated their knack for putting together a cold-weather look. (After all, Lorelai was obsessed with snow.) Rewatching the four-part follow-up a decade later sparked a deeper realization: The pair had actually been serving underrated cold-weather blueprints since the original 2000s run. So after everyone inevitably channels Lorelai and Rory this fall, consider keeping them in your style mood boards for the next season, too. Because if there’s one thing the Gilmores mastered, apart from the gift of gab, it’s styling something chic with something totally comfy.

From statement coats with chunky beanies to leather jackets and perfectly layered knits, the Stars Hollow locals knew exactly how to strike the sweet spot between cozy and cool. Ahead, I'm marking the anniversary by revisiting some of their best winter style combos — tracing their signature layering formulas from the OG series straight through to their 2016 return. Trust me, they’re just as relevant today.

Cozy, Whimsical Headwear

Rory and Lorelai have never met an accessory they didn’t like — especially when it comes to hats. From rainbow-hued berets to casual bandanas, to the occasional leopard-print cowboy hat, their headwear game is undisputed. Understandably, their winter wardrobes were no exception, and they traded their flimsier choices for thick, cold-weather knits. The more playful, the better.

In the revival, Lorelai made a case for the statement beanie when she wore a chunky gray one with an oversized pom-pom. Not one to shy away from a more-is-more philosophy, she paired it with a pastel pink coat, a cobalt blue scarf, and flared jeans — a grown-up evolution of the colorful knit caps and fuzzy hats she and Rory wore throughout the original series.

A Quiet Luxury Coat

That said, the Gilmore girls knew how to clean up nicely, too. Whether Lorelai was in a professional setting or facing her impeccably dressed (and judgmental) mother, Emily Gilmore, she knew when to tone down the playful vibe. Instead, she reached for a polished winter coat.

By the time the 2016 revival rolled around, both she and Rory were leaning heavily into sleek double-breasted numbers in solid neutral hues — like Rory’s tailored camel coat in the "Winter" episode. It was quiet luxury before the term was TikTok-famous.

Of course, a statement coat was a fave even in their earlier years on air. In one photo from the original series, both Lorelai and Rory wore structured coats with black leather gloves — elegant choices even Emily would approve of.

The Power Of A Leather Jacket

While the follow-up saw the duo trading some of their edgier staples for structured wool, rewatching it is an immediate reminder of Lorelai’s iconic original-series leather jacket collection. Motorcycle, red — you name it, she probably owned it. But Lorelai’s ultimate go-to was a leather blazer. One particularly unforgettable combo hails from the early seasons, when she paired a black blazer with a brown turtleneck top, a pencil skirt, and knee-high boots. Equal parts polished and edgy, it’s a piece that deserves a spot in anyone’s winter wardrobe rotation.

Naturally, like mother, like daughter. Rory inherited her mom’s penchant for leather, though she gave it a more collegiate, preppier twist. Case in point: her brown zip-up leather jacket paired with a plaid miniskirt, tights, and tall boots.

Lean Into The OTT

One thing about Lorelai is you could never predict her next outfit. Even a decade after the revival reminded me of her fearless approach to winter layering, she’s always been the queen of an over-the-top, maximalist moment. In one scene from the OG series, Lorelai wore a Penny Lane-coded black coat, complete with a fuzzy collar trim, to chaperone Rory and friends to a Bangles concert.

In case you needed more convincing to channel the Almost Famous icon, today’s resident cool girls are slipping back into the ‘70s-inspired coat.

Winter Style, The Stars Hollow Way

Whether you swing closer to the minimalist side of the style spectrum or the maximalist end, the A Year in the Life anniversary is the ultimate excuse to queue up a rewatch — and inject your wintry ‘fits with a little Stars Hollow charm.

item.title: Winter 2027's Top Pedicure Trends Are Anything But Boring
item.description: The biggest winter 2027 pedicure trends to know, according to experts — from mocha brown to black cherry, frosty pastels, and more.
item.dc:creator: Emma Stout
item.content:encoded:
It goes without saying that, come winter, pedicures aren’t exactly at the top of the priority list. Your toes are tucked into boots, buried under a couple layers of socks, and unlikely to see the light of day until spring. So why bother getting one?

Aside from the fact that your feet could use a little extra TLC this time of year, “there's just something about having a fresh pedicure, even when nobody else sees it,” says nail expert and Sally Beauty ambassador Juli Russell. In other words, the stakes are low — meaning you can get away with just about anything. “Keep your manicure classic and let your toes have a little more fun,” Russell says. “A pedicure is such a fun place to experiment with colors you might not normally wear.”

Maybe you’re test-driving new nail shades for summer — try cobalt blue or tomato red, both of which happen to pop against a dark winter wardrobe. Or, if you’ve been tempted by this year’s maximalist manicure trends, bedazzled designs are making their way to your toes. Partial to pastels? Lavender, baby blue, and mint are all fair game this season — with a frosty update, of course. And if you’re looking for a new neutral, consider yogurt white or mocha brown.

Whatever your vibe (or your stance on open-toed shoes in cold weather), it’s never a bad idea to treat yourself. Ahead, the biggest winter 2027 pedicure trends to try, according to the experts.

Dusty Denim

Much like your favorite pair of jeans, a denim blue pedicure never really goes out of style — but to make it feel especially wintry, opt for a shade with slightly smoky undertones.

“Denim blue brings a cool, muted feel that looks modern and understated,” says Sandra Wei, nail artist and founder of Peach Bling. “While people naturally gravitate toward warmer colors during the colder months, it offers a refreshing alternative.”

Yogurt White

If you’re partial to a white pedicure (same), there’s no need to wait until summer. “Instead of bright white, softer milky finishes are becoming popular,” says nail educator Vikki Swan.

Celebrity nail artist Elle Gerstein co-signs the milky takeover, particularly “yogurt white.” Her polish picks? Essie’s sheer white Waltz layered over Ballet Slippers, a pale pink. “It looks clean and gives a nice contrast to dark winter clothes,” she says.

Purple Gunmetal

For those already planning their New Year’s Eve pedicure, meet purple gunmetal. Less overtly festive than champagne but with plenty of shimmer and shine, it’s a shade you’ll want to wear well into January.

To get the look, layer silver chrome over a deep purple polish or reach for a multidimensional metallic like Sally Hansen’s Catch My Shift — a favorite of Russell. “The purple hue gives the industrial shade a sophisticated, feminine edge,” she says. “I especially love shades like this on toes because you get that little flash of unexpected color when the light hits.”

Mocha Brown

“Brown has been growing for a few seasons,” says nail artist and educator Viktoriia Voloshyna — but a rich, chocolatey mocha feels particularly “warm and expensive” this time of year. If black or burgundy is your go-to winter pedicure shade, consider this another contender for the season’s deep neutral. Just be sure to finish it off with an ultra-glossy top coat to really bring out the depth, according to Wei.

Frosty Pastels

Even if you’re sticking to a darker color palette for your manicures this winter, you can have a little fun with pastels on your toes. “You can play with lighter, fresher colors because they’re your own little surprise under your boots,” says Voloshyna.

To make shades like baby blue, smoky lavender, and pale mint feel less springy, celebrity nail artist and ENailCouture founder Max Estrada likes to lean into their frostier vibes. “When you add shimmering finishes, delicate crystals, or platinum-colored detailing, they suddenly feel like a winter palace,” he says.

Black Cherry
